script:
Bro, Germany के पास oil था ही नहीं…
फिर भी उनके tanks चलते रहे।

कैसे?

Simple.

उनके पास coal था।
बहुत सारा coal।

तो scientists ने कुछ ऐसा किया,
जो impossible लगता था —
coal को liquid fuel में बदल दिया।

इसका नाम था Fischer-Tropsch process.

1925 में invent हुआ,
और 1940s तक Germany की war machine
इससे बने fuel पर चल रही थी।

Leuna-Werke जैसी factories
दिन-रात fuel बना रही थीं।

अब यहाँ twist है।

ये technology मरी नहीं।

1950s में South Africa ने इसे अपनाया।
Apartheid की वजह से उस पर oil embargo था।

तो उन्होंने Sasol बनाया —
और Secunda में एक massive coal-to-liquid industry खड़ी कर दी।

आज भी ये technology इस्तेमाल हो रही है।

एक wartime जुगाड़…
जो permanent solution बन गया।

shots.intent_text: Reveal the surprising fact that German armored forces continued operating despite the oil shortage.

shots.prompt: 1920s German chemical-process diagram showing coal converted through pipes and reaction vessels, patent-era technical illustration, archival industrial documentary aesthetic, aged paper texture
shots.intent_text: Hold on the unanswered question and invite curiosity about the hidden fuel source.

music_plan.mood: Restrained industrial curiosity that builds into uneasy historical tension, then settles into reflective ambiguity
music_plan.tempo: Slow to moderate, with a subtle pulse kept well beneath narration

selected_track.attribution: "Stasis (music for space)" by Drakensson is licensed under CC BY 4.0. To view a copy of this license, visit https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.

creative_context.tone: Brisk, curious, and soberly investigative, revealing how an industrial wartime necessity became a long-lived energy technology
creative_context.audience: Hindi-speaking viewers interested in overlooked industrial, wartime, and energy-history stories
constraints: No glorified or heroic portrayal of Nazi Germany, its military, or its war machine.
No Nazi symbols used decoratively; use only where historically necessary and with contextual restraint.
No AI-generated faces or impersonations of real historical figures.
Do not aestheticize forced labor, wartime destruction, or apartheid-era oppression.
Depict apartheid as a system of racial oppression, not merely an oil-supply inconvenience.
Keep technical diagrams and maps historically sourced or clearly labeled as explanatory graphics.
creative_context.visual_style: Archival industrial documentary: 1920s chemical-process diagrams and patent-era imagery, Second World War German refinery and coal-mining records, period maps, restrained factory photographs, South African Sasol and Secunda industrial imagery, and contemporary satellite views of coal-to-liquids infrastructure
creative_context.camera_language: Static archival frames, slow map moves, restrained push-ins on factories and technical diagrams; no whip pans or flashy transitions
creative_context.historical_period: 1925 Fischer–Tropsch invention; Nazi Germany’s synthetic-fuel industry during the Second World War (1939–1945); apartheid-era South African coal-to-liquids development from the 1950s through the Secunda expansion of the late 20th century, with present-day industrial use
